assertions.statement: End-to-end neural network models have been widely applied to autonomous driving.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) learn to generate steering commands directly from front-facing camera images.
CNNs are trained on diverse driving data including video and steering inputs.
ChauffeurNet advances this approach by utilizing mid-level input representations combined with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to output driving trajectories.
ChauffeurNet enables training on both real and simulated data.
ChauffeurNet supports closed-loop simulation testing before real-world deployment.
The CARLA simulator serves as a comprehensive open-source platform that facilitates development, training, and validation of autonomous driving models.
CARLA provides flexible sensor and environment configurations along with digital urban assets.
CARLA supports evaluation of various driving approaches including end-to-end learning and reinforcement learning.
Pure imitation learning methods face significant limitations such as error accumulation and distribution shift during closed-loop operation.
These limitations lead to failures like getting stuck or collisions even with large datasets and mid-level representations.
Models like ChauffeurNet and simulators like CARLA enable closed-loop testing.
There remains a critical gap in effectively mitigating these issues.
This indicates the need for novel methods to improve robustness and reliability in autonomous driving policies trained with simulation and synthesized data.
